name: V U This interactive TV and projector walkthroughs

walkthroughs.title: Connect a Phone or Laptop to TV Without HDMI: Interactive Walkthrough
walkthroughs.description: Connect a phone, tablet or laptop to a TV or projector browser. Follow the screen-code setup, then show a PDF, photos or a message without an HDMI cable from your controller.
walkthroughs.outcome: Your chosen content on the room screen. The controls stay with you.
human_requests: How can I connect my laptop to a TV without HDMI?
Can I show phone content on a projector without casting?
search_terms: connect laptop to TV without HDMI

image.alt: A PDF on the room display with a separate phone controller

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

steps.name: Choose what the room should see
steps.text: Choose Document for a PDF, Photos for pictures, Text for a short message or another screen feature. The TV displays your selected content.
steps.outcome: You have selected the right content mode.

steps.name: Prepare the content on your controller
steps.text: Select the intended file or enter the message. Check the controller preview before you put it in front of the room.
steps.outcome: The intended content is ready.

steps.name: Choose Show now
steps.text: Tap Show now to put the selected content on the display. Keep your controls on the phone or laptop while the audience sees the result.
steps.outcome: The room sees the selected content.

steps.name: Follow the feature walkthrough
steps.text: Choose the PDF, slides, photos or screen-message guide below for the exact controls. Both devices can use different internet connections.
steps.outcome: You can change the display from the controller.

walkthroughs.success_check: You can change the display from the controller.

walkthroughs.title: Show a PDF on TV or a Projector Without HDMI: Interactive Guide
walkthroughs.description: Display a PDF on TV or a projector from your phone or laptop. Follow Document, Show now, Fit page and Fit width with an interactive page-control illustration.
walkthroughs.outcome: A clean PDF on the display, with page changes controlled from your device.
human_requests: I need to show this PDF on a projector now.
How can I display a PDF on a smart TV without a USB stick?
search_terms: display PDF on TV from phone

image.alt: A programme PDF displayed on TV with Previous, Next and view controls on a phone

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

steps.name: Choose Document and select your PDF
steps.text: On the connected controller, choose Document and select the PDF you want to present. Check that it is the intended document.
steps.outcome: The PDF is selected on the controller.

steps.name: Tap Show now to display the PDF
steps.text: Choose Show now. The PDF appears on TV or the projector while its controls remain on your phone or laptop.
steps.outcome: The audience sees the document.

steps.name: Use Fit page or Fit width
steps.text: Fit page keeps the complete page visible. Fit width enlarges a tall page for reading. Choose the view that makes the important text legible.
steps.outcome: The page is framed for your audience.

steps.name: Turn pages from your phone or laptop
steps.text: Use Previous and Next. In Fit width, the controls move through a tall page a screenful at a time before changing pages.
steps.outcome: You can present the document at your own pace.

walkthroughs.success_check: You can present the document at your own pace.

walkthroughs.title: PowerPoint, Google Slides and Keynote on TV Without HDMI
walkthroughs.description: Show PowerPoint, Google Slides, Keynote or Canva slide pages on TV or a projector. Export to PDF, connect a controller and advance slides without an HDMI cable from your laptop.
walkthroughs.outcome: Slide pages on the room screen. You decide when the next one appears.
human_requests: Put my PowerPoint slides on the TV without HDMI.
How can I show a Google Slides or Keynote presentation on this projector?

image.alt: Slide-style PDF pages on a TV with a separate controller

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

steps.name: Export your presentation as PDF
steps.text: In PowerPoint, Google Slides, Keynote or Canva, export or download the presentation as PDF. Check the exported page order and layout.
steps.outcome: Your presentation is ready as a PDF.

steps.name: Choose Document, then Show now
steps.text: Select the exported slide PDF in Document and choose Show now. The presentation pages appear on the shared screen.
steps.outcome: The first slide page is on the display.

steps.name: Choose Fit page for complete slides
steps.text: Use Fit page so the entire slide is visible. A landscape presentation usually suits a widescreen TV or projector.
steps.outcome: The whole slide is visible.

steps.name: Advance the slide pages as you present
steps.text: Use Previous and Next on the controller. Keep notes and other device activity on your laptop or phone while the room sees the selected PDF.
steps.outcome: The presentation moves at your pace.

walkthroughs.success_check: The presentation moves at your pace.

walkthroughs.title: Show Photos and Run a TV Slideshow Without Casting
walkthroughs.description: Show photos from your phone on TV without casting. Follow photo selection, order, slideshow timing, Pause, Resume, Fit and Fill in an interactive walkthrough.
walkthroughs.outcome: The photos you choose on the TV. Move through them yourself or let the slideshow run.
human_requests: Show my phone photos on the TV without casting.
I need a photo slideshow for a wedding reception screen.
search_terms: show photos on TV without casting
photo slideshow on TV from phone

image.alt: Selected photos on TV with slideshow, timing and framing controls on a phone

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

steps.name: Choose Photos and add your pictures
steps.text: Choose Photos and select the images you want everyone to see. Drag the photo list into the intended order before showing it.
steps.outcome: Only the intended photo set is selected.

steps.name: Choose Show now and check the first photo
steps.text: Tap Show now. Use Previous and Next to move through individual pictures from the controller.
steps.outcome: The selected photo appears on TV.

steps.name: Set Slideshow, timing and Start over
steps.text: Turn Slideshow on for automatic advance. Set Seconds per photo and choose Start over when the set should repeat.
steps.outcome: The photos advance at the selected pace.

steps.name: Choose Fit or Fill and control playback
steps.text: Fit keeps the whole image. Fill covers the screen and can crop edges. Pause or Resume the slideshow from your device when the room needs a closer look.
steps.outcome: Your slideshow has the intended framing and pace.

walkthroughs.title: Display Large Text and Welcome Messages on TV
walkthroughs.description: Put large text on TV or a projector from your phone. Follow Text, message size, nine positions and colours to create a readable welcome or instruction screen.
walkthroughs.outcome: One clear message, readable from across the room.
human_requests: Put a large welcome message on the TV.
Show a room-change instruction on our projector.

image.alt: A large welcome message on TV with size, position and colour controls on a phone

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

steps.name: Choose Text and write the message
steps.text: Choose Text. Enter the short message the room needs: Welcome, Registration this way, Meeting in room 4 or Back at 2:00.
steps.outcome: The message says one clear thing.

steps.name: Choose S, M, L or Max
steps.text: Use L for one large line or Max when the message should fill the screen and may wrap. S and M leave more space around the words.
steps.outcome: The message has the intended scale.

steps.name: Set the position and colours
steps.text: Choose one of nine positions and a readable text/background combination. Keep the words clear from the farthest audience position.
steps.outcome: The layout suits the screen and the room.

steps.name: Choose Show now and update when needed
steps.text: Show the message on the display. Change the wording, position or available styling from the controller when the next instruction is needed.
steps.outcome: The room has the current instruction.

walkthroughs.success_check: The room has the current instruction.

walkthroughs.title: Turn a TV into a Digital Notice Board: Interactive Walkthrough
walkthroughs.description: Display announcements on TV from your phone. Build a notice with title, subtitle and footer, preview the hierarchy and update a reception or event screen.
walkthroughs.outcome: A structured announcement that tells everyone what changed and what to do next.
human_requests: Turn the reception TV into a digital notice board.
Show a conference room-change announcement from my phone.

image.alt: A TV announcement with title, supporting text and footer beside its phone controls

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

steps.name: Choose Announcement and write the title
steps.text: Choose Announcement. Give the notice a short title such as Session change, Welcome or Today at reception.
steps.outcome: The main point is immediately clear.

steps.name: Add the subtitle and footer
steps.text: Use the subtitle for the useful detail and the footer for a time, room or next action. For example: Workshop moved to Hall B; Follow signs upstairs.
steps.outcome: The notice has a readable information hierarchy.

steps.name: Choose colours and check the layout
steps.text: Choose readable colours. If your current product access includes an image, add one when it helps explain the notice. Preview how the words fit.
steps.outcome: The important detail stands out.

steps.name: Show the notice and keep it current
steps.text: Choose Show now. Update the announcement from the controller when plans change, then clear or replace it when it no longer applies.
steps.outcome: Visitors see the current announcement.

walkthroughs.title: Show a Full-Screen Clock or World Time on TV
walkthroughs.description: Put a full-screen clock on TV and control it from your phone. Choose local time or a time zone, a clear label, 12/24-hour format, seconds and date.
walkthroughs.outcome: One large labelled clock for the time the room needs to follow.
human_requests: Put a full-screen clock on our meeting-room TV.
Show New York time on a London office screen.
search_terms: New York time on office screen

image.alt: A labelled full-screen clock on TV with time zone and format settings on a phone

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

steps.name: Choose Clock and the time source
steps.text: Choose Clock. Select Local time for the display browser time zone, or Time zone for another place.
steps.outcome: The clock follows the intended location.

steps.name: Pick the zone and add a label
steps.text: For another time zone, choose the place the room needs to follow. Add a label such as New York, London office or Event time.
steps.outcome: Everyone knows which time they are seeing.

steps.name: Set 12/24-hour format, seconds and date
steps.text: Choose the time format. Turn seconds or the date on when they are useful, and select readable colours.
steps.outcome: The time detail suits the room.

steps.name: Choose Show now
steps.text: Put the clock on the display. Change its settings from the controller while the screen keeps the time visible.
steps.outcome: The room has one clear shared clock.

walkthroughs.title: Countdown, Count-Up and Presentation Timer on TV
walkthroughs.description: Control a full-screen TV or projector timer from your phone. Explore Down, Up and To a time, with labels, Pause, Resume and Restart for meetings and workshops.
walkthroughs.outcome: A clean timer for the room, with timing controls on your device.
human_requests: Show a countdown timer on the workshop projector.
I need a meeting timer controlled from my phone, rather than a timer video.

image.alt: A full-screen break countdown on TV with timer controls on a phone

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

steps.name: Choose Timer and a mode
steps.text: Choose Down for a set duration, Up for elapsed time or To a time for a fixed clock-time target.
steps.outcome: The timer matches the activity.

steps.name: Set the duration or target and label
steps.text: Enter the duration or finishing time. Add a label such as Break, Questions, Presentation time or Group work. Choose readable colours.
steps.outcome: The room knows what the time refers to.

steps.name: Choose Show now and run the timer
steps.text: Show the timer on the shared display. The audience sees the large timer while the controller keeps its buttons.
steps.outcome: The room can follow the time.

steps.name: Pause, resume or restart the appropriate mode
steps.text: Down and Up support Pause, Resume and Restart. To a time stays tied to the fixed target. At the end of a countdown, the timer and background colours swap.
steps.outcome: The timer follows the event rather than distracting from it.

walkthroughs.success_check: The timer follows the event rather than distracting from it.

walkthroughs.title: Display a Now-Serving Number or Tally Counter on TV
walkthroughs.description: Put a live tally or now-serving number on TV and control it from your phone. Set the start, Step and label, then count up, count down or reset.
walkthroughs.outcome: The current number, large and labelled, with the controls kept off the public screen.
human_requests: Show a now-serving number on our TV.
I need a big counter that changes when I tap my phone.

image.alt: A labelled tally counter on a TV with plus, minus and Reset on a phone

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

steps.name: Choose Counter and write the label
steps.text: Choose Counter. Add a label such as Now serving, Places remaining, People checked in or Items collected.
steps.outcome: The number has clear context.

steps.name: Set the starting value and Step
steps.text: Choose where the count begins. Set Step to the amount added or subtracted by one tap: one for individuals or a larger value for batches.
steps.outcome: Each tap has the intended effect.

steps.name: Choose Show now
steps.text: Show the labelled counter on the TV or projector. Keep the increment, decrement and reset buttons on the controller.
steps.outcome: The room sees one clear current number.

steps.name: Count up, count down or Reset
steps.text: Use + Step or - Step as events happen. Reset returns to your chosen starting value. Check the display before calling the next turn.
steps.outcome: The screen follows the operator count.

walkthroughs.success_check: The screen follows the operator count.

walkthroughs.title: Display a Website QR Code on TV for Menus, Agendas and Feedback
walkthroughs.description: Show a website QR code on TV or a projector. Add the full link and a useful caption so visitors can open a menu, agenda, registration page or feedback form.
walkthroughs.outcome: One clear code on the screen, taking guests to the page they need.
human_requests: Put a QR code for our agenda on the conference screen.
Show a feedback link as a QR code on the TV.

image.alt: A large QR code on TV with a caption and separate controller fields

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

steps.name: Choose QR code, then URL
steps.text: Choose the QR-code feature and select URL for a web page. Use the current product interface for access to this feature.
steps.outcome: The QR code is set up for a website link.

steps.name: Enter the full destination address
steps.text: Enter the complete https:// or http:// address for the menu, agenda, form or other page. Check that it opens for the intended audience.
steps.outcome: The destination is correct.

steps.name: Add a caption and choose Show now
steps.text: Use a caption that explains the result, such as View today's agenda or Tell us how we did. Show the code on the display.
steps.outcome: Visitors know why they should scan.

steps.name: Test from the audience position
steps.text: Scan the displayed code with a separate phone. Confirm that it opens the intended page and the useful information is accessible.
steps.outcome: The code leads to the right next action.

walkthroughs.success_check: The code leads to the right next action.

walkthroughs.title: Show a Guest Wi-Fi QR Code on a Hotel or Meeting-Room TV
walkthroughs.description: Display a guest Wi-Fi QR code on TV. Enter authorised network details, add a clear caption and test joining from another phone for meetings, hotels and events.
walkthroughs.outcome: Guest-network joining details in one scannable code on the screen.
human_requests: Put our guest Wi-Fi QR code on the reception TV.
Help workshop visitors join the guest network from a screen.
search_terms: guest WiFi QR code on TV

image.alt: A guest Wi-Fi QR code displayed on TV with controller settings on a phone

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

walkthroughs.title: Build a Digital Signage Playlist on TV Without a New Media Player
walkthroughs.description: Create a browser digital signage playlist with photos, PDFs, text, announcements, clocks, timers, counters and QR codes. Follow Add to queue, order, Auto and Loop.
walkthroughs.outcome: One screen moving through the content you prepared, in the order the room needs.
human_requests: Rotate a welcome, photos and a programme PDF on our event TV.
Can I run a digital signage playlist in the TV browser?

image.alt: A TV showing one playlist item with an ordered Queue on a separate controller

steps.name: Open vuthis.com on the TV or projector
steps.text: Open vuthis.com in the display browser. For a projector, use its browser or the computer already connected to it. Keep the connection code on screen.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for a controller.

steps.name: Connect your phone, tablet or laptop
steps.text: Scan the screen QR code with your phone. On a laptop or tablet, open vuthis.com/r and enter the screen code. Both devices need internet; they can use different networks.
steps.outcome: The content controls are on your device.

steps.name: Create content and choose Add to queue
steps.text: Prepare an item in its feature, then choose Add to queue instead of Show now. Repeat for the photos, PDF, notice, clock, timer or QR code the display needs.
steps.outcome: Your screen content is collected in Queue.

steps.name: Drag the Queue into the right order
steps.text: Arrange the items in the sequence the audience should see. Remove outdated items. Use an item's Show now when something needs the screen immediately.
steps.outcome: The running order matches your event or venue.

steps.name: Choose manual play, Auto and Loop
steps.text: Use Play queue for manual progression. Turn Auto on for automatic advance, set Seconds per item and enable Loop when the sequence should repeat.
steps.outcome: The display follows your chosen playback pattern.

steps.name: Preview the whole sequence
steps.text: Watch the transitions. Slideshows and countdowns can hold Auto until their own finish; ordinary items use the Queue timing. The display continues until the V U This session ends.
steps.outcome: The screen is ready for the audience.

walkthroughs.success_check: The screen is ready for the audience.
